subject.title: Windows: Telegram voice-note STT + exec-approvals writer fail silently with EPERM on fsync/rename (no retry, no user feedback)

question: Should this be scoped first as a bounded reliability repair for the two verified writers, with Telegram feedback only after its failure boundary is confirmed, rather than adopting the proposed in-memory STT pipeline or a new state-directory setting?
rationale: The issue proposes four materially different solutions; only the older access-mode media failure is currently tied to a merged implementation, while retries, user messaging, streaming, and state-location configuration carry different ownership and compatibility consequences.

options.title: Verify then narrow the repair
options.body: Reproduce or trace current-main Telegram media and exec-approval writes, then add only the smallest owner-correct retry and regression coverage for confirmed transient Windows failures.

options.title: Adopt in-memory STT
options.body: Treat eliminating Telegram voice-note disk persistence as a separate product change with its own provider and attachment-contract review.

options.title: Add state relocation
options.body: Introduce a supported state-directory configuration only if diagnostics prove user-profile locking remains a broad product problem after writer-level fixes.

recommendation.title: Verify then narrow the repair
recommendation.body: Reproduce or trace current-main Telegram media and exec-approval writes, then add only the smallest owner-correct retry and regression coverage for confirmed transient Windows failures.

likelyOwner.reason: Their merged Windows media-flush work is the strongest available history signal for the closest confirmed portion of this report.
